absent: Actual mailbox or doorbell submission sequence and completion polling for platform commands beyond numeric identifiers and descriptor layouts.
Firmware error codes and retry or recovery behavior for failed launch migration or attestation flows.
Memory ownership and lifetime rules for guest context pages and firmware staging buffers beyond fallback allocation results.
Locking and concurrency rules for concurrent firmware commands and for page table dump walks.
Backend registration and persistence guarantees for stored records and erase semantics.
Precision time clock operations and timestamp conversion beyond request and snapshot layouts.

findings.text: Classic confidential guest commands use grouped numeric identifiers. Platform operations occupy values one through thirteen where initialization takes one and shutdown takes two and factory reset takes three and status takes four and platform key generation takes five and signing request takes six and certificate import takes seven and Diffie Hellman export takes eight and key generation takes nine and data flush takes ten and firmware download takes eleven and identifier retrieval takes twelve and extended initialization takes thirteen. Guest control takes thirty two through thirty five for decommission activate deactivate and status. Launch takes forty eight through fifty four for start data update save area update measurement secret injection finish and attestation. Outgoing migration takes sixty four through sixty eight for start data save area finish and cancel. Incoming migration takes eighty through eighty three for start data save area and finish. Debug takes ninety six and ninety seven.

Secure nested paging extensions use higher grouped identifiers. Initialization takes one twenty nine through one thirty four for init shutdown status data flush extended init and extended shutdown. Guest control takes one forty four through one forty nine for decommission activate status context creation guest request and extended activate. Launch takes one sixty through one sixty two for start update and finish. Debug and mitigation take one seventy six through one seventy eight for decrypt encrypt and verification. Page management takes one ninety two through one ninety five plus one ninety eight through two oh three plus two oh five and two oh six for swap out swap in move metadata init state set reclaim unsmash configuration extended firmware download commit key load and feature query. Trusted IO takes two oh eight through two thirteen for status init device create reclaim connect and disconnect. A final marker terminates the table.

Nested paging launch distinguishes page kinds by small numbers where normal takes one and save area takes two and zero takes three and unmeasured takes four and secret takes five and processor identification takes six with a maximum marker after. Capability reporting uses single bit positions where extended shutdown takes bit one and energy reporting disable takes bit two and ciphertext hiding takes bit three and wide encryption policy takes bit four and coherent link allowance takes bit five and mitigation verification takes bit thirteen, with trusted IO support also at bit one in its own word. Mitigation verification uses subcommand zero for status and one for verify. Extended initialization reserves value one to request embedded save area support.

Platform initialization descriptors carry flags plus a reserved word plus a 64 bit memory address plus a length for a reserved memory region, with the extended form adding a total length prefix plus a nonvolatile storage address and length pair for persistent state. Nested paging extended initialization instead packs single bit requests for memory integrity setup and range list enable and energy reporting disable and ciphertext hiding and trusted IO plus reserved space plus a list pointer plus a maximum identifier for nested paging address spaces plus padding. A small host side argument block carries an error code plus a probe flag plus the same maximum identifier.

Certificate and firmware transfer descriptors follow an address plus length pattern. Signing request and identifier retrieval and firmware download each pair a 64 bit pointer with a 32 bit length where some lengths update on return to report actual size. Key certificate import pairs two such pointer length groups for platform and owner certificates with a reserved word between. Diffie Hellman export pairs two pointer length groups for the key and chain each with bidirectional length and a reserved word between. The nested paging firmware download variant repeats the single pointer length pair.

Classic guest control descriptors center on a numeric handle. Decommission and deactivate carry only the handle. Activation adds an address space identifier. Status query takes a handle and returns policy and address space identifier plus a single byte state. Nested paging variants replace the handle with a 64 bit physical address of a guest context where activation pairs that address with an address space identifier and status pairs it with a reporting buffer address and a generic address holder carries one bidirectional 64 bit value.

Launch descriptors progress from creation through measurement to completion. Start takes a bidirectional handle plus policy plus certificate and session pointer length pairs with reserved spacing. Data and save area updates each take a handle plus reserved word plus a data pointer and length. Measurement takes a handle plus pointer and length where length updates to report size. Secret injection carries a handle plus three pointer length groups for header guest and transport areas with reserved words between. Finish carries only a handle. Nested paging start carries guest and migration context addresses plus policy plus single bit migration and incoming enables plus desired timer frequency plus a sixteen byte visible work area. Nested paging update carries context plus size type and incoming flags plus data address plus per level permission bytes. Nested paging finish carries context and identification and authentication addresses plus single bit enables plus reserved bits plus a thirty two byte host data field.

Migration descriptors separate outgoing and incoming flows. Outgoing start takes a handle and returns policy while supplying certificate chain and session pointer length groups with reserved spacing where session length updates on return. Outgoing data and save area updates each supply header guest and transport pointer length groups with header length updating on return. Outgoing finish and cancel each carry only a handle. Incoming start takes a bidirectional handle plus policy plus platform certificate and session pointer length groups. Incoming data and save area updates each supply header guest and transport pointer length groups without length update. Incoming finish carries only a handle.

Debug and attestation descriptors move bytes between protection domains. Classic debug carries a handle plus reserved word plus source and destination 64 bit addresses plus a length. Attestation carries a handle plus reserved word plus a report address plus a sixteen byte nonce plus a bidirectional length. Nested paging debug carries a guest context address plus source and destination addresses without explicit length in the fragment. Guest request carries a guest context address plus request and response buffer addresses.

Nested paging memory bookkeeping uses small range records with a base plus page count plus reserved word grouped into a counted list with flexible tail. Reclaim and unsmash each carry a single physical address. Shutdown extension carries a length plus single bit requests for input output unit and processor shutdown. Commit carries only a length. Feature query carries a length plus input selector plus a physical address for results where results hold four 32 bit identification words. Mitigation verification carries a length plus subcommand plus vector plus address enable bits plus optional source and destination addresses with padding, while its destination record reports verified and supported vectors plus failure status. Version records for older and newer processor families each pack boot loader trusted execution secure paging and microcode levels with reserved bytes in family specific order.

All firmware facing descriptors are tightly packed without compiler inserted gaps and use explicit reserved members to preserve wire positions. Address fields are 64 bit values paired with 32 bit lengths. Direction notes distinguish caller supplied inputs from firmware returned outputs and bidirectional lengths that the caller sizes and the firmware updates. Handles are 32 bit opaque references while nested paging contexts use 64 bit physical addresses. Boolean options in newer descriptors use single bit fields with named reserved remainder to fill the word.

When the fallback header variant applies, platform status and platform initialization and guest activation deactivation decommission data flush external command dispatch and generic command dispatch each report device absence without touching hardware, with platform initialization accepting the host argument block and status accepting a status buffer plus error slot and guest helpers accepting their corresponding descriptors plus error slot and generic dispatch accepting a command number plus opaque data plus return slot.

In the fallback variant, user blob duplication reports an invalid argument error pointer rather than copying, firmware page allocation returns a null pointer, page reclamation reports device absence, page release and platform shutdown perform no action, and ciphertext hiding support query reports false. Reclamation accepts a physical address plus page count plus a locked flag while allocation accepts allocation flags and blob duplication accepts a user address plus length.

Security processor messaging reserves low sixteen bits for status, next eight bits for command, next six bits as reserved, then a recovery bit and a response bit at the top. A busy value of thirteen indicates an already initialized ring. Doorbell messaging reuses the command field for message content and uses bit zero for ring selection.

Physical address translation for security processor buffers has two build variants where one routes through memory encryption aware translation and the other uses the direct kernel mapping translation, selected by configuration rather than runtime choice.

Persistent storage backends distinguish record kinds by small numbers where kernel log takes zero and machine check takes one and console takes two and function trace takes three and platform records take four through six and eight with user message at seven and a maximum marker after. Capability flags use single bits for log console trace and user message support. Function trace storage reserves low bit masks for processor number where one variant uses value one and another uses value three, plus an eight bit shift and derived mask for packing processor number into timestamps.

A stored record bundles a backend pointer plus a kind plus an identifier plus a timestamp plus a data buffer and size plus error correction notice size plus private state plus a count plus a dump reason plus a part number plus a compression flag. Backend information holds an owner and name plus a buffer and size plus capability flags plus maximum reason plus private data. A function trace entry holds an instruction address plus a caller address plus a timestamp.

Backend information protects its staging buffer and size with a raw spinlock suitable for constrained contexts, while read side traversal is serialized by a mutex held across open through close sequences.

Backends expose entry points for opening and closing a read session plus reading one record plus writing a kernel record plus writing from user memory plus erasing a record, where read fills the supplied record object and write consumes it and user write additionally takes a user pointer.

Two build variants encode processor identity and time differently. One folds the processor number into low bits of the instruction address while leaving the timestamp word untouched and decodes by masking the address. The other preserves the address and packs the processor number into low timestamp bits while shifting the true time upward, decoding by masking for the processor and shifting for time and updating by preserving the unaffected portion.
Page table dumping bounds a walk with an address interval carrying a start and an end, grouped with a state object that carries the active interval pointer.

Dumping state exposes callbacks invoked per level for entries at each hierarchy depth plus a flush hook plus protection decoding hooks per level, allowing hosts to observe mappings without owning the walk.

Debugging of writable executable mappings is gated so the check runs only when the corresponding configuration is enabled, otherwise doing nothing. Page table isolation initialization and finalization are empty hooks in this header variant.

Precision time requests select among external timestamp and periodic output and pulse per second modes and carry a discriminated payload for the first two modes. System timestamp capture pairs snapshots taken before and after device access with a clock identifier. Clock names are bounded to thirty two bytes including termination.

Callers must size bidirectional lengths before firmware calls because firmware updates them and undersized buffers truncate certificates measurements and session data. User supplied blobs and session pointers require validation and copying since firmware addresses are physical. Firmware page allocation can fail and reclamation requires correct locking state. Attestation nonces must be unique per request and secret injection must keep header guest and transport buffers distinct. Persistent trace encoding loses low address or timestamp bits to processor packing so decoding must use the matching variant.
Each header uses a once only inclusion guard that defines a unique macro on first inclusion to prevent repeated processing.

Platform lifecycle moves from initialization through steady operation to shutdown or factory reset, with data flush and firmware download and status queries available while operational. Guests move from launch start through data and measurement updates to finish, then between active and deactive states, with attestation and debug available while bound and decommission ending the binding. Migration splits into outgoing start update finish or cancel and incoming start update finish sequences. Nested paging mirrors this with context creation launch update finish activation and page state transitions plus commit.
